module purpose: This module implements a depth-configurable queued buffer with separate write and read pointers: it stores input words from wdata_i, returns stored words on rdata_o, and reports occupancy and access status. Depending on the generics, it can qualify read/write requests with avail/free, register the read/status outputs, and reset the whole storage array.

use-case flows.value: qualified write and read requests that the FIFO will actually accept
read/write pointer state update, including clear-to-zero and accepted increment
payload word written into FIFO storage when a write is accepted
stored payload word returned on rdata_o from fifo_reg or fifo_mem
occupancy count and status flags (level, free, avail, half)
pointer state cleared by rstn_i and clear_i, with optional storage and synchronous-status reset

conceptual assets.concept: Buffered payload word values stored by the queue and returned on rdata_o
conceptual assets.reasoning: The data flow stores wdata_i into fifo_reg when fifo_depth_c = 1 (lines 134-135 or 170-171) or into fifo_mem at the selected write position when fifo_depth_c > 1 (lines 149-150 or 183-184). The read-out flow returns fifo_reg directly (lines 201, 232) or fifo_mem selected by the read-pointer path (lines 213, 241) on rdata_o. Integrity is established because the module defines this value's storage and delivery path to its output; corruption changes the word delivered at the boundary. Availability is also established conditionally because the written value is held in fifo_reg/fifo_mem between writes and exposed on the implemented read path; when FULL_RESET is true the storage is forced to zero on rstn_i (lines 131-147).

conceptual assets.concept: Qualified write and read operation decisions
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module computes the accepted operations as `re <= re_i when (FIFO_SAFE = false) else (re_i and avail);` (line 64) and `we <= we_i when (FIFO_SAFE = false) else (we_i and free);` (line 65). These decisions control whether the pointers advance (lines 82-83) and whether payload storage is written (lines 134-150, 170-184). Integrity is established because incorrect qualification changes when the queue consumes or produces state updates and payload writes. Availability is also established under the RTL-visible conditions: requests propagate directly when FIFO_SAFE = false, and when FIFO_SAFE = true they propagate only while avail/free permit them.

conceptual assets.concept: Read and write position state that determines which storage location is used next
conceptual assets.reasoning: The stored position state is held in w_pnt and r_pnt: rstn_i clears them to zero (lines 72-74), they take w_nxt and r_nxt on each rising edge (lines 75-77), and those next values either clear to zero on clear_i, increment on accepted write/read, or hold (lines 82-83). w_pnt selects which fifo_mem entry is written (lines 150, 184), r_pnt or its registered async copy r_pnt_ff selects which entry is read out (lines 210, 213, 241), and pointer comparisons also drive match/full/empty/level (lines 92-95, 102-105). Integrity is established because correct storage selection, retrieval position, and occupancy computation depend on this state. Availability is also established because the position state is preserved across cycles and can be forced to a known zero state by rstn_i or clear_i.

The module computes occupancy as `level <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(w_pnt) - unsigned(r_pnt));` for fifo_depth_c > 1 (line 95) or all copies of full for fifo_depth_c = 1 (line 105). It derives `half` from level/full (lines 96, 106), `free` from `not full` (line 110), and `avail` from `not empty` (line 111). These values are reported through level_o (lines 116-117) and through free_o/avail_o/half_o either combinationally (lines 217-219) or synchronously with reset values when FIFO_RSYNC is true (lines 249-256). Integrity is established because these are module outputs, and free/avail also qualify the accepted operations when FIFO_SAFE is true (lines 64-65). Availability is established because the RTL continuously or clockedly produces these reports in the selected configuration.
